title: All-level Padic Tor vanishing implies ambient flat cohomology
statement: Let T be noetherian, of bounded Krull dimension, with l invertible in every stalk. Let E/Q_l be finite and K a bounded constructible intrinsically complete complex for the actual unlifted Padic valuation-ring datum [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. If the higher Tor condition [prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations] holds above every cutoff for the canonical reduction tower, then every cohomology sheaf H^q(K) is flat over the completed coefficient ring, in the exact-tensor-functor sense [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. This is only the converse implication of the original criterion.

proof.text: Fix q and apply the local torsion normal-form theorem, which assumes no Tor vanishing. Obtain a finite stratification, covering charts, and H^q(K)|_U isomorphic to F plus N, where every section module of F has a finite basis. The lemma also supplies a nilpotent endomorphism f of N and a quotient map from a pulled-back Tor_1 sheaf to cokernel f.

Specialize the all-cutoff Tor hypothesis to cutoff q-1, degree q, and p=1, at the supplied quotient index. Its Tor sheaf is zero, and exact pullback and scalar restriction preserve zero. Its epimorphic image cokernel f is therefore zero. Hence f is epic. Every power of f is epic, including a power equal to zero by nilpotence. This forces N=0. This categorical argument does not need a nonempty chart or nonzero residue sheaf.

A finite basis makes each section module of F free, hence flat. Apply the module equational criterion to every restricted finite relation; the maximal covering sieve supplies the local sheaf equational criterion. Thus F is flat on the site. Transport flatness across the cohomology isomorphism and the biproduct-with-zero isomorphism.

For each monomorphism of ambient module sheaves, form the kernel of its tensor with H^q(K). Exact ring-module pullback and naturality of the ordinary tensor comparison identify its pullback with a zero kernel on every stratum-cover chart. Forget modules to additive sheaves, using the adjunction-unit comparison to identify module inverse image with additive inverse image. Noetherian stratum detection makes the ambient kernel zero. Tensor preserves colimits and is additive, so preservation of monomorphisms gives left exactness; together with right exactness this is site flatness.

proof_origin.place: Original steps 2 and 8: complete kernel-descent proof, after separating the independent DVR normal form. The torsion obstruction is discharged by nilpotent epimorphisms rather than nonzero residue sections.

theorem pbc_adic_tor_implies_flat_cohomology
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian T]
    (_hdim : ∃ n : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim T ≤ n)
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type (u + 1)) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (_hl : ∀ t : T, IsUnit (l : T.presheaf.stalk t))
    (K : PbcBoundedConstructibleComplete T (pbcPadicCoefficientDatum l E)) :
    (∀ m : ℤ, PbcLevelwiseTorVanishing T (pbcPadicCoefficientDatum l E)
        (pbcReductionAdicTower T (pbcPadicCoefficientDatum l E) K.obj) m) →
      ∀ q : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlatOnSite (J := ProEt.topology T)
        (R := pbcAdicCompletion T (pbcPadicCoefficientDatum l E))
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K.obj)
